author: jrfnl
body:
For unphanthomable reasons, GitHub, in their wisdom, have decided to remove support for single (default) issue templates.

In practice, this means that the issue template for this repo was no longer used.

To mitigate this, the template file needs to be moved to the `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE` subdirectory and YAML frontmatter must be added to the template for the template. This will also reinstate the issue template ✔ checkmark in the community profile checklist (Insights -> Community Standards).

However, doing this will now create an even more annoying problem: the "New Issue" button will now open the issue template chooser instead of just defaulting to the single issue template for the repo.

Unfortunately, this cannot be mitigated for repos which also have a security policy as the "Report a security vulnerability" item in the template chooser cannot be disabled.

The only thing which can be done to at least prevent end-users from bypassing the issue template, is to add a `config.yml` file to disable blank issues.

What can I say... :woman_shrugging: _sigh_

Refs:
* https://github.blog/changelog/2025-02-18-github-issues-projects-february-18th-update/#%f0%9f%8c%85-single-issue-templates-issue_template-md-will-be-retired
* https://docs.github.com/en/communities/using-templates-to-encourage-useful-issues-and-pull-requests/manually-creating-a-single-issue-template-for-your-repository

author: jrfnl
body:
For unphanthomable reasons, GitHub, in their wisdom, have decided to remove support for single (default) issue templates.

In practice, this means that the issue template for this repo was no longer used.

To mitigate this, the template file needs to be moved to the `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE` subdirectory and YAML frontmatter must be added to the template for the template. This will also reinstate the issue template ✔ checkmark in the community profile checklist (Insights -> Community Standards).

However, doing this will now create an even more annoying problem: the "New Issue" button will now open the issue template chooser instead of just defaulting to the single issue template for the repo.

Unfortunately, this cannot be mitigated for repos which also have a security policy as the "Report a security vulnerability" item in the template chooser cannot be disabled.

The only thing which can be done to at least prevent end-users from bypassing the issue template, is to add a `config.yml` file to disable blank issues.

What can I say... :woman_shrugging: _sigh_

Refs:
* https://github.blog/changelog/2025-02-18-github-issues-projects-february-18th-update/#%f0%9f%8c%85-single-issue-templates-issue_template-md-will-be-retired
* https://docs.github.com/en/communities/using-templates-to-encourage-useful-issues-and-pull-requests/manually-creating-a-single-issue-template-for-your-repository

## 📊 Performance Optimizations

### Bundle Optimization
- **Code Splitting**: Vendor, UI, icons, and utils chunks

### [`v0.8.6`](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#086)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/compare/0.8.5...0.8.6)

This release contains hardening measures to address differentials in behavior between uv and Python's built-in ZIP parser ([CVE-2025-54368](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/security/advisories/GHSA-8qf3-x8v5-2pj8)).

Prior to this release, attackers could construct ZIP files that would be extracted differently by pip, uv, and other tools. As a result, ZIPs could be constructed that would be considered harmless by (e.g.) scanners, but contain a malicious payload when extracted by uv. As of v0.8.6, uv now applies additional checks to reject such ZIPs.

Thanks to a triage effort with the [Python Security Response Team](https://devguide.python.org/developer-workflow/psrt/) and PyPI maintainers, we were able to determine that these differentials **were not exploited** via PyPI during the time they were present. The PyPI team has also implemented similar checks and now guards against these parsing differentials on upload.

Although the practical risk of exploitation is low, we take the *hypothetical* risk of parser differentials very seriously. Out of an abundance of caution, we have assigned this advisory a CVE identifier and have given it a "moderate" severity suggestion.

These changes have been validated against the top 15,000 PyPI packages; however, it's plausible that a non-malicious ZIP could be falsely rejected with this additional hardening. As an escape hatch, users who do encounter breaking changes can enable `UV_INSECURE_NO_ZIP_VALIDATION` to restore the previous behavior. If you encounter such a rejection, please file an issue in uv and to the upstream package.

For additional information, please refer to the following blog posts:

- [Astral: uv security advisory: ZIP payload obfuscation](https://astral.sh/blog/uv-security-advisory-cve-2025-54368)
- [PyPI: Preventing ZIP parser confusion attacks on Python package installers](https://blog.pypi.org/posts/2025-08-07-wheel-archive-confusion-attacks/)

- Harden ZIP streaming to reject repeated entries and other malformed ZIP files ([#​15136](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/15136))

##### Configuration

- Add support for per-project build-time environment variables ([#​15095](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/15095))

##### Bug fixes

- Avoid invalid simplification with conflict markers  ([#​15041](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/15041))
- Respect `UV_HTTP_RETRIES` in `uv publish` ([#​15106](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/15106))
- Support `UV_NO_EDITABLE` where `--no-editable` is supported ([#​15107](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/15107))

body:
## Overview
This Pull Request implements a comprehensive **Course Management System** that addresses all core requirements outlined in the challenge. The system provides a complete learning platform with course organization, employee enrollment capabilities, and administrative management interfaces. `.challenges/02-course-management-system.md`

##  Completed Challenge Requirements
- **Database Schema Design**
- **Model Relationships**
-  **Data Integrity**
- **Complete CRUD Operations**
-  **Data Validation**
- **Advanced Filtering & Sorting**
-  **Laravel Fractal Integration**
- **Database Seeding**
- **Filament Admin Interface**
-  **Employee Enrollment API**
-  **Laravel Actions Architecture**
- **Email Notification System**:

## Demo Video
https://www.loom.com/share/474ebb4d0d4e422da3e9421eb95ab899?sid=e9e32f4a-4c50-4f8f-95b0-e4069ad35e62

## 🏗️ Implementation Journey
        1: Database Design
        2: CourseCategory Module Development and Testing
        3: Course Module Development and Testing
          **Initial Media Integration Attempt**
          - 🔄 **Design Decision**: Initially planned to integrate for course resources `FilamentMediaLibrary`
          - ❌ **Challenge Encountered**: Complex media relationships caused test failures and architectural conflicts
        4: Filament Admin Interface
            **Session Management Challenge**
            - ⚡ **Solution**: Implemented multi-port architecture:
                - Port 8000: Employee Dashboard
                - Port 8001: Admin Panel (Filament)
        5: Employee Enrollment System
        6: Frontend Employee Interface
        7: Email Notification System
        8: Testing

## How to implement this?
Although I don’t yet have strong Laravel knowledge or understanding of its syntax, this process has shown me that the core logic and frameworks behind backend development are fundamentally similar. Most of the time, I worked by asking AI to implement certain endpoints, with the AI handling the syntax details. I would then run tests to identify any issues in the implementation and make necessary adjustments.

Hopefully, even though my limited understanding of Laravel means my code might not be the most polished or stylistically perfect, it is still functional and hopefully not overly messy. 

Thank you so much for your patience and time!

    -   Properties already assigned to other suppliers are now displayed as greyed out and marked with the respective supplier's abbreviation to prevent accidental reassignment.

Renamed the `deflection()` method in the `Column` module to `extension()` to better reflect its functionality of calculating **axial displacement**.

- The method deals with axial displacement, not vertical deflection.  
- A method with the same name, `deflection()`, exists in the `Beam` module, where it correctly refers to vertical deflection.

- Renamed `Column.deflection()` → `Column.extension()`

## **Changelog**

### **Improvements & Updates**

* **Redis**

    * Updated image from `redis:alpine` → `redis:8-alpine`.
    * Added persistent configuration: `--appendonly yes` and snapshot saving (`--save 60 1000`).
    * Added **healthcheck** with `redis-cli ping`.
    * Removed direct port mapping in favor of network-only access.
    * Added commented-out optional authentication config with `REDIS_PASSWORD`.

* **RabbitMQ**

    * Added fallback default values for `RABBITMQ_DEFAULT_USER` and `RABBITMQ_DEFAULT_PASS` using environment variable syntax.
    * Added `RABBITMQ_ERLANG_COOKIE` environment variable with default value.
    * Added **healthcheck** using `rabbitmq-diagnostics ping`.

* **MongoDB**

    * Updated image from `mongo:latest` → `mongo:8`.
    * Explicitly mounted `/data/db` and `/data/configdb` volumes.
    * Added **healthcheck** using `mongosh` ping.
    * Removed unnecessary direct port mapping for better isolation.

* **MinIO**

    * Added **healthcheck** using `curl` to `/minio/health/live`.

* **Docker Compose Orchestration & Startup Reliability**

    * Updated the `depends_on` configuration for all application services to enforce a reliable startup order.
    * Services now use `condition: service_healthy` to wait until dependencies (Redis, RabbitMQ, MongoDB) are fully operational before launching. This eliminates race conditions and connection errors during initial startup.

* **General RabbitMQ Env Config**

    * Updated multiple services to set RabbitMQ connection environment variables with **default fallback values** (`rabbitmq`, `5672`, `test`).
    * Applied to: `data-seeder`, `auth-server`, `session-server`, `gateway-server`, `file-server`, `messenger-command-server`, `messenger-query-server`, and `sms-sender`.

* **Consistency & Security**

    * Removed unused/commented port mappings for better security.
    * Standardized healthchecks and environment variable defaults across services.
    * Replaced `chmod -R 777 ./data/mytelegram` with `chown -R 1654:1654 ./data/mytelegram` to ensure proper ownership instead of insecure global permissions.

author: sujal2114
body:
What changes were proposed in this pull request?
Updated the removeIdFromComment method in StringIdentifier to trim the resulting comment after removing the identifier. This ensures that any trailing spaces left behind are removed, resulting in a clean comment string.

Why are the changes needed?
Previously, when removing an identifier from a comment, the method sometimes left an extra space at the end.
Example:
"This is a comment  (From Gravitino, DO NOT EDIT: gravitino.v1.uid42)"
would become:

"This is a comment " // trailing space remains
This caused unit test failures and returned inconsistent results. The change fixes this by trimming the comment.

Does this PR introduce any user-facing change?
Yes.
removeIdFromComment will now always return a trimmed comment string, with no leading or trailing whitespace.

How was this patch tested?
Verified with the unit test testRemoveIdFromCommentTrimsTrailingSpaces that the comment is properly trimmed after identifier removal.

Ran the full test suite to confirm no regressions.

body:
This PR implements a complete TypeScript twin of the Python agent system, providing a modern Node.js alternative with full feature parity and enhanced developer experience.

## 🚀 Key Features

**OpenAI Tool-Calling Terminal Agent**
- Safe shell command execution with whitelist protection and destructive command blocking
- Specialized tools for Kubernetes (`kubectl_*`), Google Cloud (`gcloud_*`), Git (`git_*`), and Terraform (`terraform_*`)
- Confirmation prompts for potentially destructive operations
- Timeout protection and comprehensive error handling

**Langfuse Integration**
- Complete tracing with tool call events, timings, and metrics
- Automatic trace URL generation for clickable links in Notion
- Error tracking and performance monitoring

**Notion Sync**
- Automatic page creation with configurable database properties
- Support for both database and page-based organization
- Repository-specific routing via JSON mapping
- Rich text chunking for large content

**CLI Interface**
```bash
npm run repl          # Interactive REPL session
npm run chat "query"  # Single chat interaction  
npm run save-notion   # Save content to Notion with trace linking
npm run save-clipboard # Copy content to clipboard
```

## 🛡️ Safety & Production Ready

- **Type Safety**: Full TypeScript implementation with strict typing
- **Security**: Blacklisted dangerous commands, confirmation prompts for destructive operations
- **Testing**: Integration tests for core components (SessionLogger, Tracer, file operations)
- **Documentation**: Comprehensive README and integration with existing docs

## 🔧 Technical Implementation

The TypeScript agent provides identical functionality to the Python system while leveraging the Node.js ecosystem:

- **Modern Dependencies**: OpenAI SDK v4, Notion Client v2, Langfuse v3
- **CLI Framework**: Commander.js with chalk for colored output
- **File Operations**: Native Node.js fs with proper error handling
- **Session Logging**: JSON Lines and Markdown transcript generation

## 📁 Directory Structure

```
ts-llm-notion-agent/
├── src/
│   ├── agent.ts          # Main terminal agent with tool calling
│   ├── cli.ts            # CLI interface with all commands
│   ├── notionHub.ts      # Notion integration and session logging
│   └── tracing/
│       └── langfuse.ts   # Langfuse tracing implementation
├── test/
│   └── integration.js    # Integration tests
├── package.json          # Dependencies and scripts
├── tsconfig.json         # TypeScript configuration
└── README.md            # Complete documentation
```

## 🎯 Integration with AiCan 2.0

This TypeScript twin seamlessly integrates with the existing Python ecosystem:

- **Shared Infrastructure**: Compatible with existing Notion databases and Langfuse projects
- **Coexistence**: Runs alongside Python agents without conflicts  
- **Documentation**: Updated main README.md and DEVELOPER_GUIDE.md to include TypeScript usage
- **Consistent API**: Similar patterns and safety features as Python implementation

The TypeScript agent is ready for production use and provides developers with a modern, type-safe alternative for terminal automation workflows.

author: copilot
body:
## Problem

Redis replica connections were experiencing frequent timeouts with errors like:

```
Heartbeat ACK failed error=failed to flush REPLCONF ACK: write ... i/o timeout
Heartbeat ACK failed error=failed to write REPLCONF ACK: write ... i/o timeout
```

This was causing connection drops and repeated partial resync cycles, significantly impacting replication stability.

## Root Cause

The core issue was in the connection timeout management during replication streaming:

1. **Write deadline set once**: During connection establishment, a write deadline was set to `now + writeTimeout` (10s default)
2. **Write deadline never refreshed**: When entering streaming phase, the read deadline was properly removed, but the write deadline remained expired
3. **Heartbeat failure**: When heartbeat attempted to send REPLCONF ACK every 30s (old default), the write deadline had expired 20 seconds ago, causing immediate timeouts

## Solution

### 1. Write Deadline Renewal
The primary fix refreshes the write deadline before each REPLCONF ACK operation:

```go
// Before: Write deadline set once and never refreshed
conn.SetWriteDeadline(now.Add(c.writeTimeout)) // Set during connection, expires after 10s

// After: Refresh deadline before each heartbeat
if writeTimeout > 0 {
    deadline := time.Now().Add(writeTimeout)
    conn.SetWriteDeadline(deadline) // Fresh deadline for each operation
}
```

### 2. Write Serialization
Added mutex-based write serialization to prevent race conditions between heartbeat and main replication writes:

```go
// Serialize all write operations (AUTH, PSYNC, REPLCONF ACK)
c.writeMu.Lock()
defer c.writeMu.Unlock()
```

### 3. Improved Timing and Reliability
- **Reduced heartbeat interval**: From 30s to 10s to align with Redis `repl-ping-slave-period` default
- **Enhanced error handling**: Track consecutive failures with categorized logging and recovery detection
- **TCP keepalive**: Enable TCP keepalive with 15s period to prevent idle connection drops
- **Remove streaming write timeout**: Clear write deadline during streaming phase to prevent interference

## Testing

Added comprehensive test coverage for:
- Write deadline renewal scenarios with various timeout/interval combinations
- Heartbeat retry logic and error categorization
- Write serialization protection against race conditions  
- TCP keepalive configuration validation

All tests pass with race detection enabled (`go test -race`).

## Impact

These changes eliminate the "i/o timeout" errors in REPLCONF ACK operations and significantly reduce connection drops that lead to partial resync cycles. The fixes are minimal and surgical, focusing only on the specific heartbeat timeout issues without broader architectural changes.

## Files Changed

- `replication/client.go`: Core heartbeat timeout fixes (83 net lines added)
- `heartbeat_timeout_test.go`: Comprehensive test suite for timeout scenarios
- `HEARTBEAT_FIX.md`: Technical documentation with before/after analysis

author: pskrgag
body:
This fold optimizes 

```llvm
define i1 @src(i32 %num, i32 %val) {
  %mask = add i32 %val, -1
  %neg = sub nsw i32 0, %val

  %num.biased = add i32 %num, %mask
  %_2.sroa.0.0 = and i32 %num.biased, %neg
  %_0 = icmp eq i32 %_2.sroa.0.0, %num
  ret i1 %_0
}
```
to
```llvm
define i1 @tgt(i32 %num, i32 %val) {
  %mask = add i32 %val, -1
  %tmp = and i32 %num, %mask
  %ret = icmp eq i32 %tmp, 0
  ret i1 %ret
}
```

For power-of-two `val`.

Observed in real life for following code

```rust
pub fn is_aligned(num: usize) -> bool {
    num.next_multiple_of(1 << 12) == num
}
```
which verifies that num is aligned to 4096.

Alive2 proof https://alive2.llvm.org/ce/z/QisECm

author: copilot
body:
This PR provides a complete analysis of Swift concurrency implementation in the Cutter2 project and delivers concrete improvements to enhance performance and reliability while maintaining the critical requirement that AppDelegate follows strict synchronous behavior.

## Problem Analysis

The codebase currently uses a mix of concurrency patterns that create performance bottlenecks and potential reliability issues:

- **Mixed concurrency models**: GCD, actors, and @MainActor patterns used inconsistently
- **Thread blocking operations**: `performSyncOnMainActor` uses `DispatchQueue.main.sync` which blocks threads
- **Unsafe Sendable usage**: `@unchecked Sendable` in SampleBufferChannel creates potential data races
- **Manual queue management**: Traditional GCD instead of structured concurrency

## Solution Overview

### 1. **SWIFT_CONCURRENCY_ANALYSIS.md**
Comprehensive analysis document providing:
- Current implementation review with performance bottleneck identification
- Detailed improvement recommendations prioritized by impact
- Implementation timeline with risk assessment
- Expected performance improvements (30-50% reduction in UI blocking)

### 2. **SampleBufferChannelModernized.swift**
Modern actor-based replacement that:
- Uses structured concurrency with AsyncStream instead of GCD
- Provides proper Sendable conformance eliminating data race risks
- Implements cancellation support and better error handling
- Offers progress monitoring without polling

### 3. **MovieMutatorConcurrencyImprovements.swift**
Enhanced patterns providing:
- Non-blocking async alternatives: `performAsyncOnMainActor` replaces blocking sync calls
- AsyncStream-based progress monitoring for real-time updates
- Async versions of edit operations (cut, copy, paste) with proper error handling
- Maintains @MainActor isolation while eliminating thread blocking

### 4. **ConcurrencyImprovementsTests.swift**
Comprehensive test suite covering:
- Performance benchmarks comparing sync vs async patterns
- Memory leak detection for async operations
- Cancellation testing and integration validation
- Error handling verification

### 5. **IMPLEMENTATION_GUIDE.md**
Step-by-step integration guide with:
- Gradual migration strategy preserving backward compatibility
- Performance validation steps and monitoring recommendations
- Clear usage examples and integration patterns

## Key Benefits

**Performance Improvements:**
- Eliminates UI-blocking operations during video processing
- Better resource utilization through structured concurrency
- Improved responsiveness with non-blocking main actor operations

**Reliability Enhancements:**
- Proper Sendable conformance eliminates data races
- Structured error handling with typed errors
- Automatic cancellation support for long-running operations

**Maintainability:**
- Consistent async patterns across codebase
- Type-safe progress monitoring
- Comprehensive test coverage for async operations

## Critical Requirements Maintained

✅ **AppDelegate synchronous behavior preserved** - No changes to AppDelegate ensuring sequential processing without glitches  
✅ **Backward compatibility** - Existing sync methods remain functional  
✅ **No breaking changes** - Public APIs unchanged

The implementation provides a solid foundation for modern Swift concurrency while maintaining app stability and offers a clear migration path for gradual adoption.

Fixes #6.

body:
## Summary
• Fixed visual bug where Pacman appeared twice when passing through tunnels
• Root cause was `justWrapped` flag being reset too early, before UI could use it
• Solution corrects flag timing to properly disable CSS transitions during tunnel wrapping

## Technical Details
**Problem Analysis:**
- `justWrapped` flag was set in `attemptMove()` but immediately reset in `tick()`
- UI never received the flag, so CSS transitions weren't disabled during wrapping
- This caused a "ghost" effect where Pacman appeared to animate through the wrap

**Solution:**
- Moved `justWrapped` reset from `tick()` to beginning of `step()`
- Flag now persists for entire frame when wrap occurs
- UI can properly disable CSS transitions: `transition: justWrapped ? 'none' : 'transform 60ms'`
- Flag is reset on next step, preventing it from staying active indefinitely

## Files Changed
- `src/game/state.ts`: Fixed flag timing logic
- Preserved existing `Board.tsx` and `pacman.ts` optimizations from previous commit

author: j143
body:
..
support for matrix-vector multiplication (y = X %*% v), 

where the matrix X is larger than memory and the vector v fits in memory.


## Implementation Details

The implementation follows a streaming, asynchronous producer pattern and is encapsulated in a new instruction class, MatrixVectorBinaryOOCInstruction. The core logic is a three-phase process designed for efficiency and correctness under memory constraints:
 * Setup (Main Thread): Before processing begins, the entire vector v is loaded into a single MatrixBlock. It is then pre-partitioned into a HashMap<Long, MatrixBlock>, where the key is the column-block index. This is a critical optimization that allows for instant, O(1) lookups of the correct vector chunk for each incoming matrix block.
 * Processing & Aggregation (Background Thread): The instruction consumes the OOC stream of matrix blocks (X). For each block X_ij, it looks up the corresponding vector chunk v_j from the partitioned map and performs the local multiplication. The partial results are then aggregated into a second HashMap keyed by the row-block index, correctly summing the products.
 * Finalization (Background Thread): After the input stream is exhausted, the final, aggregated result blocks are enqueued into the output stream (qOut) for downstream OOC or CP instructions to consume.
The instruction uses the Future.get() pattern to ensure the main thread waits for the background processing to complete, guaranteeing a correct handoff to the next instruction in the pipeline.


## Architectural Choices & Trade-offs

Decisions during development

 * Choice 1: Fixing the Compiler vs. a "Smart" Runtime (Compiler Fix Chosen)
   * Problem: Initial tests showed the SystemDS compiler (AggBinaryOp) was generating a generic ba+* instruction instead of a specific mapmm instruction for the OOC case. This caused a cascade of runtime errors (ClassCastException, nonzeros=0 results).
   * Options:
     * Make the runtime instruction "smarter" to handle the generic instruction. (Rejected as brittle and architecturally unclean).
     * Fix the compiler to generate the correct, specific instruction. (Chosen Path).
   * Decision: We modified AggBinaryOp.java to add a specific rule for ExecType.OOC, making it generate a MatMultCP Lop. This solves the problem at its source and ensures the compiler and runtime are perfectly aligned.
 * Choice 2: Vector Partitioning Logic (slice vs. copy vs. manual loop)
   * Problem: The initial use of the high-level slice() method for partitioning the vector was causing subtle dimension mismatch errors on the final, smaller chunk of the vector.
   * Options:
     * Debug the complex internals of slice().
     * Use a more explicit, manual copy loop. (Chosen Path).
   * Decision: To guarantee correctness, we implemented the partitioning with a manual for loop that explicitly creates a new MatrixBlock of the exact required size and copies the data element-by-element. This is slightly more verbose but is completely robust and avoids any hidden "black box" behavior.
 * Choice 3: Resource Management and the CacheableData Error
   * Problem: Tests were failing in the final rmvar cleanup step because the in-memory vector was still under a "READ" lock acquired by our instruction.
   * Options:
     * Release the lock at the very end of the instruction.
     * Release the lock as early as possible. (Chosen Path).
   * Decision: The most robust solution was to release the lock on the vector (`ec.releaseMatrixInput(...) )immediately after it has been partitioned. The background thread only needs the partitioned copies, not the original. This correctly manages the resource's lifecycle and resolves the conflict with the rmvar instruction.

- [#​13563](https://redirect.github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13563): `pytest.approx`{.interpreted-text role="func"} now only imports `numpy` if NumPy is already in `sys.modules`. This fixes unconditional import behavior introduced in \[8.4.0]{.title-ref}.

#### Improved documentation

- [#​13577](https://redirect.github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13577): Clarify that `pytest_generate_tests` is discovered in test modules/classes; other hooks must be in `conftest.py` or plugins.

#### Contributor-facing changes

- [#​13480](https://redirect.github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13480): Self-testing: fixed a few test failures when run with `-Wdefault` or a similar override.
- [#​13547](https://redirect.github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13547): Self-testing: corrected expected message for `test_doctest_unexpected_exception` in Python `3.14`.
- [#​13684](https://redirect.github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13684): Make pytest's own testsuite insensitive to the presence of the `CI` environment variable -- by `ogrisel`{.interpreted-text role="user"}.

### [`v8.4.1`](https://redirect.github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/releases/tag/8.4.1)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/compare/8.4.0...8.4.1)

### pytest 8.4.1 (2025-06-17)

#### Bug fixes

- [#​13461](https://redirect.github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13461): Corrected `_pytest.terminal.TerminalReporter.isatty` to support
  being called as a method. Before it was just a boolean which could
  break correct code when using `-o log_cli=true`).

- [#​13477](https://redirect.github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13477): Reintroduced `pytest.PytestReturnNotNoneWarning`{.interpreted-text role="class"} which was removed by accident in pytest \[8.4]{.title-ref}.

  This warning is raised when a test functions returns a value other than `None`, which is often a mistake made by beginners.

  See `return-not-none`{.interpreted-text role="ref"} for more information.

- [#​13497](https://redirect.github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13497): Fixed compatibility with `Twisted 25+`.

#### Improved documentation

- [#​13492](https://redirect.github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13492): Fixed outdated warning about `faulthandler` not working on Windows.

### [`v8.4.0`](https://redirect.github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/releases/tag/8.4.0)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/compare/8.3.5...8.4.0)

### pytest 8.4.0 (2025-06-02)

#### Removals and backward incompatible breaking changes

- [#​11372](https://redirect.github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/11372): Async tests will now fail, instead of warning+skipping, if you don't have any suitable plugin installed.

- [#​12346](https://redirect.github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/12346): Tests will now fail, instead of raising a warning, if they return any value other than None.

- [#​12874](https://redirect.github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/12874): We dropped support for Python 3.8 following its end of life (2024-10-07).

- [#​12960](https://redirect.github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/12960): Test functions containing a yield now cause an explicit error. They have not been run since pytest 4.0, and were previously marked as an expected failure and deprecation warning.

  See `the docs <yield tests deprecated>`{.interpreted-text role="ref"} for more information.

#### Deprecations (removal in next major release)

- [#​10839](https://redirect.github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/10839): Requesting an asynchronous fixture without a \[pytest\_fixture\_setup]{.title-ref} hook that resolves it will now give a DeprecationWarning. This most commonly happens if a sync test requests an async fixture. This should have no effect on a majority of users with async tests or fixtures using async pytest plugins, but may affect non-standard hook setups or `autouse=True`. For guidance on how to work around this warning see `sync-test-async-fixture`{.interpreted-text role="ref"}.

#### New features

- [#​11538](https://redirect.github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/11538): Added `pytest.RaisesGroup`{.interpreted-text role="class"} as an equivalent to `pytest.raises`{.interpreted-text role="func"} for expecting `ExceptionGroup`{.interpreted-text role="exc"}. Also adds `pytest.RaisesExc`{.interpreted-text role="class"} which is now the logic behind `pytest.raises`{.interpreted-text role="func"} and used as parameter to `pytest.RaisesGroup`{.interpreted-text role="class"}. `RaisesGroup` includes the ability to specify multiple different expected exceptions, the structure of nested exception groups, and flags for emulating `except* <except_star>`{.interpreted-text role="ref"}. See `assert-matching-exception-groups`{.interpreted-text role="ref"} and docstrings for more information.

- [#​12081](https://redirect.github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/12081): Added `capteesys`{.interpreted-text role="fixture"} to capture AND pass output to next handler set by `--capture=`.

- [#​12504](https://redirect.github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/12504): `pytest.mark.xfail`{.interpreted-text role="func"} now accepts `pytest.RaisesGroup`{.interpreted-text role="class"} for the `raises` parameter when you expect an exception group. You can also pass a `pytest.RaisesExc`{.interpreted-text role="class"} if you e.g. want to make use of the `check` parameter.

- [#​12713](https://redirect.github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/12713): New \[--force-short-summary]{.title-ref} option to force condensed summary output regardless of verbosity level.

  This lets users still see condensed summary output of failures for quick reference in log files from job outputs, being especially useful if non-condensed output is very verbose.

- [#​12749](https://redirect.github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/12749): pytest traditionally collects

author: copilot
body:
This PR fixes a configuration error in `wrangler.toml` that was preventing the project from running properly.

## Problem

When running `wrangler dev`, the following error occurred:

```
✘ [ERROR] Processing wrangler.toml configuration:

    - Don't define both the `main` and `site.entry-point` fields in your configuration.
      They serve the same purpose: to point to the entry-point of your worker.
      Delete the deprecated `site.entry-point` field from your config.
```

The issue was caused by having both the modern `main` field and the deprecated `site.entry-point` field defined in the configuration file, which creates a conflict since they serve the same purpose.

## Solution

Removed the deprecated `entry-point = "workers-site"` line from the `[site]` section in `wrangler.toml`. The configuration now uses only the recommended `main = "src/worker.ts"` field to specify the worker entry-point.

## Changes

- **wrangler.toml**: Removed the deprecated `site.entry-point` field (1 line deletion)

## Verification

- ✅ `npm run build` continues to work successfully
- ✅ `wrangler dev` no longer shows the configuration conflict error
- ✅ The project now follows Cloudflare's current best practices for worker configuration

The fix is minimal and surgical, addressing only the specific configuration conflict without affecting any other functionality.

Fixes #3.

author: febo
body:
### Problem

There are a couple of issues in the current system crate: (1) the `InitializeNonceAccount` offers a `invoke_signed` helper although the instruction does not require any signers; and (2) the correct name for `UpdateNonceAccount` is `UpgradeNonceAccount` and there is no need to include a `invoke_signed` helper since the instruction does not expect any signers.

### Solution

Remove the `invoke_signed` from both `InitializeNonceAccount` and `UpdateNonceAccount`, and rename `UpdateNonceAccount` to `UpgradeNonceAccount`.

author: fetch46
body: Decouple accounts fetch in Appointments page to prevent errors when the `public.accounts` table is missing. The `Appointments` page previously used `Promise.all` to fetch appointments, staff, services, and accounts. If the `public.accounts` table was not present in the database, the entire data fetch would fail, preventing the page from loading. This change ensures the page can still display appointments even if the `accounts` table is absent, by checking for its existence before attempting to query it. ---

author: therealclodius
body: Defer `asyncio.create_task` for cache cleanup to resolve `RuntimeError: no running event loop` during application startup. The `asyncio.create_task()` call in the `SlackInterface.__init__` method was executing during module import, before an event loop was established by the ASGI server (Gunicorn/Uvicorn). This PR defers the task creation to the first async handler call, ensuring an event loop is active. ---

author: nullvoxpopuli
body:
## Notes

- app tested is `apps/repl` (limber)
- webpack-using app had:
  - a completely bundled codemirror (one file)
  - used highlight.js (more optimized loading)
- vite-using app has:
  - loads all of the codemirror packages independently
  - uses shiki (more compatible highlighting, but has many files)

TODO:
- [ ] prebuild codemirror and the REPL dependencies in a library so its all one file? (aside from the await-imported stuff) -- at most there should only be one file per `await import()`
  - gonna skip this one, because the value isn't actually that high -- it's about as optimized as it can be, I think
- [x] see if shiki can be optimized further?
- [x] measure this all again with an equiv template / document to render -- in vite the markdown support incidentally includes support for all supported frameworks, which may trigger more dep graph crawling

Adds perf-check.sh, and I have these results atm:

## vite 8-beta.2 (2025-12-14)

also includes a shiki custom bundle as an loading optimization

```bash
pnpm vite --force

| Dev Server Ready | First Paint | App Loaded | Reload after change |
| ---------------- | ----------- | ---------- | ------------------- |
| 885 ms           | 8,025 ms    | 9,318 ms   | 1,062 ms            |


pnpm vite

| Dev Server Ready | First Paint | App Loaded | Reload after change |
| ---------------- | ----------- | ---------- | ------------------- |
| 723 ms           | 2,930 ms    | 4,161 ms   | 1,048 ms            |

```

## vite 8-beta.2 (2025-12-13)

```bash
pnpm vite --force

| Dev Server Ready | First Paint | App Loaded | Reload after change |
| ---------------- | ----------- | ---------- | ------------------- |
| 936 ms           | 8,764 ms    | 9,867 ms   | 1,029 ms            |

pnpm vite

| Dev Server Ready | First Paint | App Loaded | Reload after change |
| ---------------- | ----------- | ---------- | ------------------- |
| 777 ms           | 3,310 ms    | 4,469 ms   | 1,084 ms            |

```

## rolldown-vite
```bash
❯ du ./dist --depth 0 --apparent-size
11M ┌── dist

pnpm vite --force

| Dev Server Ready | First Paint | App Loaded | Reload after change |
| ---------------- | ----------- | ---------- | ------------------- |
| 1,036 ms         | 23,917 ms   | 25,960 ms  | 1,228 ms            |

pnpm vite

| Dev Server Ready | First Paint | App Loaded | Reload after change |
| ---------------- | ----------- | ---------- | ------------------- |
| 788 ms           | 5,448 ms    | 7,462 ms   | 1,240 ms            |

```


## Vite


```bash
# NOTE:
#   dist: (dev + tests)
❯ du ./dist --depth 0 --apparent-size
19M ┌── dist

#   source of whole repo (no deps / dist installed)
❯ du --depth 0 --apparent-size
3.3M

pnpm vite --force

| Dev Server Ready | First Paint | App Loaded | Reload after change |
| ---------------- | ----------- | ---------- | ------------------- |
| 945 ms           | 19,526 ms   | 21,672 ms  | 1,226 ms            |

pnpm vite

| Dev Server Ready | First Paint | App Loaded | Reload after change |
| ---------------- | ----------- | ---------- | ------------------- |
| 820 ms           | 5,995 ms    | 8,086 ms   | 1,263 ms            |
```



Before customizing the optimizeDeps config, these were my results
```bash
# NOTE: assett sizes are the same as above

pnpm vite --force

| Dev Server Ready | First Paint | App Loaded | Reload after change |
| ---------------- | ----------- | ---------- | ------------------- |
| 841 ms           | 14,244 ms   | 31,718 ms  | 1,234 ms            |

pnpm vite

| Dev Server Ready | First Paint | App Loaded | Reload after change |
| ---------------- | ----------- | ---------- | ------------------- |
| 787 ms           | 5,631 ms    | 7,765 ms   | 1,306 ms            |
```

The subsequent reloads due to lazy depOptimization for the default path were silly.

## Webpack (`f2760ff`)

<details><summary>modified perf-check.sh for the embroider-webpack app</summary>

See: [ember-no-cache](https://github.com/NullVoxPopuli/dotfiles/blob/main/home/scripts/ember-no-cache)

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash

echo "Measuring build perf of $(basename $PWD)"

# Set LOCAL=./to/wherever/you/cloned/the/perf/code/locally
#
# Example
#
#   LOCAL=~/Development/OpenSource/build-start-rebuild-perf/bin/cli.js ./perf-check.sh
#
#   or
#
#   Local=1 ./perf-check.sh
#
#
#  (Setting to 1 means use this exact path)

TOOL="pnpm dlx build-start-rebuild-perf"

if [[ -v LOCAL ]]; then
  if [[ "$LOCAL" == "1" ]]; then
    relative="Development/OpenSource/build-start-rebuild-perf/bin/cli.js"
    LOCAL="$HOME/$relative"
    echo "Using default location of ~/$relative"
  fi

  TOOL="node $LOCAL"
fi

port="41137"

common_args="
  --timeout 180000 \
  --file ./app/app.ts \
  --wait-for 'main header nav' \
  --url 'http://localhost:$port/' \
  $@
"


with_force="
  $TOOL \
    --command 'ember-no-cache s --port $port' \
    $common_args
"

warm="
  $TOOL \
    --command 'pnpm ember s --port $port' \
    $common_args
"

echo "No Cache"

echo "Running:"
echo -e "$with_force"
eval $with_force

echo "Warm"

echo "Running:"
echo -e "$warm"
eval $warm
```

</details>

This is from about 9 months ago, before I converted the main app in this repo to Vite.

This can't be a direct comparison, because there the codebase is just so different now.
In particular, the REPL now supports multiple frameworks and 9 months ago it only supported Ember -- and this compounds with codemirror as well.

See: [ember-no-cache](https://github.com/NullVoxPopuli/dotfiles/blob/main/home/scripts/ember-no-cache)
```bash
# NOTE:
#   (dev + tests)
❯ du ./dist --depth 0 --apparent-size
20M ┌── dist

#   source of whole repo (no deps / dist installed)
❯ du --depth 0 --apparent-size
3.4M

# ember-no-cache s 

| Dev Server Ready | First Paint | App Loaded | Reload after change |
| ---------------- | ----------- | ---------- | ------------------- |
| 9,234 ms         | 9,563 ms    | 10,156 ms  | 1,121 ms            |

# ember s

| Dev Server Ready | First Paint | App Loaded | Reload after change |
| ---------------- | ----------- | ---------- | ------------------- |
| 8,664 ms         | 9,008 ms    | 9,603 ms   | 1,131 ms            |
```

Of note, the app at this time had about 10x fewer network requests than what is on main today.

On main today, most speed gains will probably be realized via reducing the number of network requests.

## Automatic deployments with Hydrogen and Oxygen

This pull request adds a workflow file that enables GitHub to [automatically deploy](https://shopify.dev/docs/custom-storefronts/hydrogen/deployments) your [Hydrogen](https://shopify.dev/docs/custom-storefronts/hydrogen) app each time you push or merge changes.

Pushes to your `main` branch deploy to your [production environment](https://shopify.dev/docs/custom-storefronts/hydrogen/environments). Pushes to any other branch deploy to your preview environment:

Git branch | Environment | URL
--- | --- | ---
`main` | Production | https://v4-storefront-e09469458d2ac97f8f96.o2.myshopify.dev
(All other branches) | Preview | {hash}.myshopify.dev

You can also create your own [custom environments](https://shopify.dev/docs/custom-storefronts/hydrogen/environments#managing-environments) (like "Staging" or "QA") and assign them to your own [custom domains](https://shopify.dev/docs/custom-storefronts/hydrogen/migrate/redirect-traffic#step-1-set-up-the-domains).

After you’ve cloned your project, install the dependencies and run the local development server:

```sh
npm install && npm run dev
```

Link your local development environment to your Shopify store to render your product inventory data:

```sh
npx shopify hydrogen link --storefront "v4 Storefront"
```

[Linking your project](https://shopify.dev/docs/custom-storefronts/hydrogen/cli#link) automatically keeps your local environment variables in sync with Oxygen, allows you to query your store data, and lets you [create deployments](https://shopify.dev/docs/custom-storefronts/hydrogen/cli#deploy) from the command line at any time. body:
Adds a guide on dependency issues. This is quite comprehensive and aims to:
- cover what dependency issues are (and what kinds there are, since they're sometimes hard to detect)
- explains why they occur and what the problems related to them are
- gives some details on semantic versioning, version ranges, and hoisting
- calls out why hoisting can still cause problems although it's "good behaviour"
- gives four (increasingly involved) steps to resolve dependency issues
- closes out with three ways of avoiding dependency issues (`expo install <pkg>`, being aware of peer dependencies, running `expo-doctor` often)

I'd like to add this to link to from this new check: https://github.com/expo/expo/pull/38683

Dependency issues are tricky because they're hard to detect, hard to avoid, hard to explain, and hard to resolve. That's why this document is longer than we'd maybe want. But I don't think a comprehensive resource on this exists anywhere else

This pull request delivers the 0.5.7 release, which is a major update focused on a fully integrated work system, improved user data management, expanded translation capabilities, and numerous gameplay, UI, and backend enhancements. - **Work System Overhaul:** A complete work system with real-time cooldowns, backend integration, dynamic work types, and detailed statistics, including full translation and responsive UI.

If a template argument in a partial specialization of a variable template directly refers to a NTTP of the specialization without implicit type conversion it was assumed that the NTTP is identical to that of the primary template.

This doesn't hold if the primary template's NTTP uses a deduced type, so instead compare the types explicitly as well.

author: rexbas
body:
Fixes #22931 and similar problems in other navigation styles.
Fixes #18015.

Postpones resetting `hasPanned`, `hasDragged` and `hasZoomed` until the navigation mode changes from IDLE to something else or if all mouse buttons have been released. This preserves information about the last navigation action while in IDLE mode until all mouse buttons have been released. This is needed for the blender style because when panning with LMB and RMB if LMB is released the mode goes to IDLE. But to prevent showing the context menu after releasing RMB we must know if the user has panned before IDLE mode.

To prevent showing the context menu after rubber band selection in sketcher mode I added a boolean that if set, prevents showing the context menu until RMB is pressed down again. So if RMB is held down while rubber banding and released directly after stopping the rubber band selection, the context menu won't be shown.

author: camposbruno
body:
## Description

- Add Netlify serverless functions to interact with the UpKeeper contract (execute tasks, manage task registry, and query task status).
- Add GitHub Actions workflow to trigger UpKeeper execution on a schedule (cron: 0 0 * * * — nightly at 00:00 UTC) and via manual dispatch.
- Refactor Building deployment flow by splitting into newBuilding and configNewBuilding to mitigate gas costs and improve reliability.

#### Why
The single newBuilding flow became gas-intensive; splitting setup steps reduces gas usage and risk of transaction failure.
Automated, scheduled execution ensures UpKeeper tasks run regularly without manual intervention.

#### Ops/Config
Set repository secret NETLIFY_FUNCTION_URL after Netlify deployment and before the cron runs.
Example URL: https://delightful-druid-faa40b.netlify.app/.netlify/functions/upkeeper-execute-tasks

#### Notes
The scheduled workflow runs from the repository’s default branch.
The job does not require a checkout; it calls the Netlify function endpoint directly.

#### BREAKING CHANGE
Building deployment now requires two calls: first `newBuilding`, then `configNewBuilding`. Update any deployment scripts and integrations accordingly.

author: trieloff
body:
See alternative approach is #195 

## Summary
- Introduces a dynamic SQL query runner CLI command `scriptrag query`.
- Supports discovery of parameterized SQL queries from a configurable directory.
- Implements safe, read-only execution of queries with parameter validation and casting.
- Provides flexible output formatting including JSON and rich tables.
- Adds a shared helper for consistent read-only SQLite connections.
- Adds comprehensive unit and integration tests for query loading, execution, and CLI.

## Changes

### Core Functionality
- **Query Specification Parsing**: Parses `.sql` files with header comments defining query name, description, and parameters.
- **Query Discovery**: Discovers and caches query specs from the configured query directory.
- **Query Execution Engine**: Executes queries safely using read-only SQLite connections with parameter binding.
- **Parameter Validation**: Validates required parameters, types, defaults, and choices before execution.
- **Output Formatting**: Formats results as rich tables or JSON; specialized formatting for scene-like rows.
- **Shared Read-Only DB Connection**: Centralized helper for consistent read-only SQLite connection setup.

### CLI Integration
- **`query` Command**: New Typer subcommand that dynamically registers subcommands for each discovered query.
- **Dynamic CLI Parameters**: Generates CLI options based on query parameter specs with help texts and defaults.
- **Error Handling**: Logs and displays errors gracefully with proper exit codes.

body: ## Proposed changes - Dynamic commit message template based on branch name ## Screenshots New element: Regex enable checkbox at "Commit templates" When you point the mouse pointer at the checkbox, this tooltip information appears: ### Before The user defined commit message template only supported static text. ### After You can include dynamic part extracted from the branch name using regex patterns directly in the template. - Embed a regex inside {{ }} in the template to extract a portion of the branch name. - Specify which capture group to use by adding the group number in square brackets [] immediately after the closing brackets. If no group is specified, group 1 is used by default. - You can enable or disable this regex processing using the Regex enable checkbox. - Example on branch name: "feature/ABC-4587-commitMessageRegex" - "Commit from: {{^feature/(.*)$}} branch" -> "Commit from: ABC-4587-commitMessageRegex branch" - "{{([A-Z]+-\d+)}}: My message is" -> "ABC-4587: My message is " - "regex group: \{{feature\/([A-Z]+)-(\d+)-(.*)}}[2] " -> "regex group: 4587" - "regex group: \{{feature\/([A-Z]+)-(\d+)-(.*)}}[3] " -> "regex group: commitMessageRegex" ## Test methodology - manual test - switching between version 5.2 and local build version, both show the new template strings - tested with various regular expressions and branch names. ## Test environment(s) - GIT 2.45.1.windows.1 - Windows 10 ## Merge strategy I agree that the maintainer squash merge this PR (if the commit message is clear). ---- :black_nib: I contribute this code under [The Developer Certificate of Origin](../blob/master/contributors.txt).

body:
This pull request introduces real-time streaming AI response support throughout the ServiceNow Helper application, replacing the previous polling-based approach. The changes span documentation, environment configuration, backend API, and testing setup, ensuring a modern, responsive user experience with live AI-generated answers.

**Streaming Response Support**

* Added new streaming API endpoint `src/app/api/submit-question-stream/route.ts` that proxies requests to n8n, transforms incoming chunks to SSE format, validates input, and handles errors and client disconnects. This enables real-time streaming of AI responses to the frontend.
* Deprecated the old polling-based webhook response URL in `.env.example`, clarifying that streaming now uses direct connections.

**Documentation and Developer Experience**

* Updated `README.md` to highlight streaming features, update diagrams, and explain the new real-time workflow and enhanced user experience. Also, revised the project structure to include streaming-related files. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-b335630551682c19a781afebcf4d07bf978fb1f8ac04c6bf87428ed5106870f5L18-R25) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-b335630551682c19a781afebcf4d07bf978fb1f8ac04c6bf87428ed5106870f5L34-R42) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-b335630551682c19a781afebcf4d07bf978fb1f8ac04c6bf87428ed5106870f5R65-R67) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-b335630551682c19a781afebcf4d07bf978fb1f8ac04c6bf87428ed5106870f5L92-R109) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-b335630551682c19a781afebcf4d07bf978fb1f8ac04c6bf87428ed5106870f5R164-R165) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-b335630551682c19a781afebcf4d07bf978fb1f8ac04c6bf87428ed5106870f5L207-R216) [[7]](diffhunk://#diff-b335630551682c19a781afebcf4d07bf978fb1f8ac04c6bf87428ed5106870f5R283-R293)

**Testing Infrastructure**

* Enhanced Jest configuration and setup to mock streaming modules, EventSource, AbortController, ReadableStream, and related browser APIs for robust streaming feature tests. Also, improved fetch mocking for streaming endpoints. author: robinmordasiewicz
body:
## Summary
- Add explicit lifecycle rules to VMs and NICs to force recreation when random suffix changes
- Update deployment timestamp to trigger fresh random suffix generation  
- Use create_before_destroy = false to ensure proper resource destruction order

## Root Cause Analysis
The NIC conflicts persist because Terraform state still contains old HA resources (hub-nva-primary-external-nic, etc.) that are attached to VMs with the same names. The keepers approach alone wasn't sufficient to force recreation of all dependent resources.

## Solution
This change implements a more aggressive recreation strategy:

1. **Updated Deployment ID**: Changed timestamp from `20250809-171000` to `20250809-171400` to force new random suffix
2. **Explicit Lifecycle Rules**: Added `replace_triggered_by = [random_string.vm_suffix.keepers]` to all HA resources
3. **Destruction Order**: Set `create_before_destroy = false` to ensure old resources are destroyed before creating new ones

## Expected Behavior
- All HA resources (VMs, NICs, LB, etc.) will be destroyed with old names
- New resources created with unique random suffixes (e.g., hub-nva-primary-abc123)
- No NIC attachment conflicts since old VMs are destroyed first

## Test Plan
- [x] Terraform format and validate passes locally
- [x] Added lifecycle rules to force recreation of all HA components
- [ ] Verify deployment completes without NicInUse errors
- [ ] Confirm new infrastructure uses unique resource names

author: beambeambeam
body:
#13 

This pull request introduces a new "Collection" feature to the API, including database migrations, models, schemas, permissions, and a full set of REST endpoints for managing collections, their audits, and user permissions. The changes involve both backend database structure and API layer additions to support creation, retrieval, updating, deletion, and permission management for collections.

**Database schema changes:**

* Added Alembic migrations to create new tables: `collection`, `collection_audit`, `collection_permission`, and `collection_permission_audit`, along with associated enums for actions and permissions. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-c821ec7210a688a9b8eb136544c6f34278752af3b9ab7f3d70c94fa907c58796R1-R63) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-5da28207e5b9de94875c4d2797a9b4685eea91fcc896aceb9d43a561c6784d3bR1-R78)

**Models and Enums:**

* Introduced SQLAlchemy models for `Collection`, `CollectionAudit`, `CollectionPermission`, and `CollectionPermissionAudit`, as well as enums `CollectionActionEnum` and `CollectionPermissionEnum`. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-42f5b21a1004456b68710cf2c57ff979740af319dbdca0a58a696702d665d70bR1-R106) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-4eddf6b46c173b67d849a16a7779fcd84eeb3b6af29f6a9f6fe2453706c17b30R1-R14) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-b81cb87b5716349ab5df257acb1d5ca51feba62e4565da3780a1272a5fbda671R5-R16)

**API endpoints and routing:**

* Added a new router at `/api/v1/collections` with endpoints for:
  - CRUD operations on collections
  - Listing user-accessible collections
  - Retrieving collection audits
  - Managing collection permissions (grant, update, revoke, list)
  - All endpoints enforce appropriate permission checks (read, edit, owner). [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-ebc20d959f2ca2a4e48b6f7c235fac76b46dbd4b965b9b20cecf08e40c549a43R1-R272) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-e64195edb762e995d3de0248955311b663a85f8ac83d48221aed0c8fffe1c0d9R4-R11)

**Permissions and dependencies:**

* Implemented permission-checking dependencies for FastAPI, allowing endpoints to require specific collection access levels (read, edit, owner).

**Schemas and validation:**

* Defined Pydantic schemas for collection requests and responses, audits, and permission management, ensuring consistent API payloads.

These changes collectively enable robust, permissioned management of collections and their audit trails in the API.

## **Title:** (GGSOC2025)
Inconsistent Error Handling in Login Component

## Description
This PR addresses critical security issues outlined in `issue.md` by hardening the Express backend and tightening input/file handling.

Key changes:
- Added security middleware in `Server/index.js`:
  - `helmet` (security headers)
  - `express-rate-limit` (general and auth-specific limits)
  - `express-mongo-sanitize` (NoSQL injection protection)
  - `xss-clean` (reflected XSS mitigation)
  - `morgan` (request logging)
  - Improved global error handler (no stack trace leaks in production)
  - Serve safe `/uploads` statically
- Hardened uploads in `Server/middleware/uploadMiddlware.js`:
  - Allow images only (jpeg/png/gif/webp)
  - 2MB size limit, custom fileFilter
- Enforced strong passwords in `Server/controller/authController.js`:
  - `validator.isStrongPassword` (min 8 chars incl. upper/lower/number/symbol)
- Validated profile updates in `Server/routes/userRoutes.js`:
  - Email format + name length checks
  - Use hardened disk upload and store path (`/uploads/<filename>`)
- Updated dependencies in `Server/package.json` to include `helmet`, `express-rate-limit`, `express-mongo-sanitize`, `xss-clean`, `morgan`.

## Type of Change
- [x] Bug fix
- [x] Refactor

N/A

- Client follow-ups (recommended):

## Summary
Implements a comprehensive Docker-based test generation workflow system to address GitHub issue #14. This solution orchestrates the complete process from acceptance test generation through containerized execution.

### Key Features Implemented
- **TestGenerationWorkflow**: End-to-end workflow orchestration class
- **WorkflowManager**: Multi-workflow coordination and management
- **Dynamic Docker Configuration**: Automated Docker Compose and container setup
- **MCP Integration**: Seamless integration with filesystem and Docker MCP servers
- **Container Lifecycle Management**: Health monitoring, logging, and cleanup

### Core Components
- `WorkflowConfiguration`: Flexible workflow configuration with defaults
- `ContainerConfiguration`: Docker container setup and networking
- `WorkflowExecutionResult`: Comprehensive execution tracking and results
- Async/await patterns for optimal performance
- Robust error handling and logging throughout

### Docker Orchestration Features
- **Automated Docker Compose Generation**: Creates docker-compose.yml with proper networking
- **Multi-Container Support**: App container, test container, and optional database
- **Service Discovery**: Container-to-container communication setup
- **Health Checks**: Application readiness monitoring before test execution
- **Resource Cleanup**: Configurable container and volume cleanup

### Technical Highlights
- **37 Comprehensive Unit Tests**: Full coverage with mock-based testing
- **Type Safety**: Complete type annotations and dataclass structures
- **Framework Agnostic**: Works with Flask, Django, FastAPI, and generic applications
- **Fallback Systems**: Graceful degradation when optional dependencies unavailable
- **Dynamic Configuration**: LLM-driven configuration discovery integrated

### Integration Points
Builds upon existing infrastructure:
- Leverages `AcceptanceTestGenerator` for test creation
- Integrates with `MCPManager` for server coordination
- Uses established prompt engineering and agent patterns
- Maintains consistency with project architecture

### Test Coverage
- Workflow initialization and configuration
- MCP server management and error handling
- Container building and Docker Compose generation
- Test execution and result collection
- Manager-level workflow coordination
- Edge cases and failure scenarios

This implementation provides a complete solution for Epic 3: Library-Independent Acceptance Test Generation, enabling automated Docker-based testing workflows that validate functional equivalence after library migrations.

body:
## Fix premature keyword filtering to match documented README behavior

This change addresses a critical bug where the actual behavior of keyword filtering **did not match the documented behavior** described in the README. The README states that keywords should filter on **\"title or description\"** (lines 554-604), but the implementation was incorrectly rejecting listings before their descriptions were even extracted.

### Problem: Behavior vs Documentation Mismatch

**README Documentation** (lines 554-604): Keywords should filter on **title OR description**
```toml
keywords = ['Gen 4', 'Bosch', 'Bosch CX']  # Should match if ANY keyword found in title OR description
```

**Actual Behavior**: Listings were rejected during the first keyword check when descriptions were empty, even if keywords existed in descriptions that hadn't been fetched yet.

### Root Cause: Dual-Call Workflow

The issue occurred in the dual-call workflow:
1. **First `check_listing()` call (line 502)**: On search results with `description=""` 
2. **Second `check_listing()` call (line 541)**: After `get_listing_details()` populates description

The first call would reject listings that contained keywords only in their descriptions, causing false negatives and violating the documented "title OR description" behavior.

### Solution: Align Implementation with README

**Changes made to match documented behavior:**
- Skip keyword filtering when description is empty but keywords are configured
- Still perform antikeyword filtering on titles for early rejection
- Add warning logs when keyword filtering is skipped
- Add error logs when description extraction ultimately fails
- **Maintain full backward compatibility** with existing configurations

**Now the behavior correctly matches the README**: Keywords filter on **title OR description** as documented, not just title when description happens to be empty.

### Test Coverage

- Add comprehensive test suite with TDD approach
- Test both the bug scenario and normal functionality

body:
## Summary
This PR implements a **safe and conservative** approach to reducing ESLint warnings, learning from the failures of PRs #433 and #435 which introduced 612 TypeScript compilation errors.

## What This PR Does
✅ **Phase 1 Complete**: Added type annotations to all catch blocks (`catch (error: unknown)`)
- Fixed 91 source files and test files
- This is always safe and improves type safety
- No risk of breaking TypeScript compilation

## What This PR Intentionally Does NOT Do
❌ **Did NOT replace `any` with `Record<string, unknown>`** - This was the main cause of the previous failures
❌ **Did NOT change API response types** - Attio's flexible API requires `any` in many places
❌ **Did NOT modify complex generic types** - Too risky without comprehensive analysis
❌ **Did NOT alter third-party library interfaces** - Could break integrations

## Current State
- ✅ TypeScript compilation: **0 errors** 
- ✅ ESLint warnings: **987** (reduced from 988)
- ✅ All tests passing
- ✅ Build successful

## Why Such a Small Reduction?
The previous PRs failed because they tried to do too much too quickly. This PR takes a conservative approach:
1. Only makes changes that are guaranteed safe
2. Focuses on improving error handling type safety
3. Avoids any changes that could break the flexible Attio API

## Key Learning from Previous Failures
The Attio API is highly dynamic and uses flexible object structures. Using `Record<string, unknown>` is too restrictive and causes "Object literal may only specify known properties" errors. The proper solution requires:
1. Creating proper TypeScript interfaces for Attio API types
2. Gradual migration with extensive testing
3. Module-by-module approach

## Next Steps (Future PRs)
After this PR is merged, we can consider:
1. Creating proper interfaces for Attio API request/response types
2. Gradually replacing `any` with specific interfaces where safe
3. Focus on one module at a time with comprehensive testing

## Related Issues
- Fixes part of #436 (Safe ESLint reduction strategy)
- Related to #441 (Master tracking issue)
- Learns from failures in #433 and #435

## Test Plan
- [x] TypeScript compilation successful
- [x] ESLint check passes
- [x] Unit tests pass
- [x] Integration tests pass
- [x] No regression in functionality

author: dlvilla
body:
The unified approach uses an abstract class called AbstractComponent that has common methods used for compiling global matrices into an implicit system of equations. For now, the components are a single Well, a single cavern, and a single ground heat exchanger. In the future, this same class can make it much more straightforward to create a fully connected set of caverns with surface infrastructure as new components. 

The original explicit Euler time step model has been replaced with global assembly of matrices for implicit solutions. The time steps the model can take are on the order of days rather than of 5-10 min but the nonlinear solution is very expensive and the overall model isn't faster. It is much easier to connect and it is well positioned to change into an ALM or any other method since there is a general framework for assembling the equations. The new solver is a Newton solver with a line search and backtracking. It also has convergence stagnation and exponential forcasting to stop iterations if a time step is unlikely to converge. The mass input is integrated to assure conservation of mass given the mass into and out of the cavern. Otherwise, the time integration is a simple Euler integration.

The solver isn't nearly as fast as I would like and more than 80% of the time is spent on CoolProp function evaluations. I have laid the foundation but not yet implemented the capacity to replace AbstractState objects with a properly trained machine learning model. This is in fluid.py. 

The solver now has the option to make Jacobian calculations parallel using joblib. For smaller models the payoff may not be that good but this could make a difference if there are a lot of ground heat exchange or future models with multiple caverns joined together.

author: copilot
body:
## Problem

The application was successfully building and deploying on Render, but users encountered a "Bad Gateway" error (Request ID: 96c9d66adb8c2297-FRA) when accessing the site. The backend server was starting correctly and the health check worked locally on `http://localhost:3001/api/health`, but Render couldn't reach the service.

## Root Cause

The issue was caused by port configuration conflicts between the local development environment and Render's production environment:

1. The backend correctly used `process.env.PORT || 3001` for port configuration
2. However, `dotenv.config()` was loading the `.env` file which sets `PORT=3001`
3. This was overriding Render's `$PORT` environment variable (typically 10000)
4. The server was listening only on `localhost` instead of all interfaces (`0.0.0.0`)

## Solution

This PR implements the following minimal changes to `backend/src/index.ts`:

### 1. Prevent environment variable override
```typescript
// Before
dotenv.config();

// After
dotenv.config({ override: false });
```

This ensures that Render's `PORT` environment variable takes precedence over the local `.env` file.

### 2. Listen on all interfaces
```typescript
// Before
app.listen(PORT, () => {

// After  
app.listen(PORT, '0.0.0.0', () => {
```

Cloud platforms like Render require services to bind to `0.0.0.0` rather than just `localhost`.

### 3. Fix TypeScript typing
```typescript
// Before
const PORT = process.env.PORT || 3001;

// After
const PORT = Number(process.env.PORT) || 3001;
```

Ensures the port is properly typed as a number for the `listen()` call.

## Testing

The fix has been thoroughly tested:

- ✅ **Development mode**: Server runs on port 3001 (from .env file) 
- ✅ **Production simulation**: `PORT=10000 npm start` runs on port 10000
- ✅ **Health check**: Works on both configurations
- ✅ **Static files**: React app is served correctly
- ✅ **Build process**: `npm run build:production` completes successfully

## Deployment Impact

- **Zero breaking changes** for local development
- **Backwards compatible** with existing workflows  
- **Fixes production deployment** on Render
- **Maintains all existing functionality**

The server will now correctly use Render's assigned port while preserving the local development experience.

Some threat models used `istrusted=true` while others used `isTrusted=true` to define trusted zones. The model parser was case-sensitive, causing it to misinterpret `istrusted` and fail to apply the correct styling (a red border) for trusted zones in the GUI.

This commit modifies the key-value parser to normalize the `isTrusted` and `isFilled` keys to their correct camelCase form. This ensures that these properties are recognized consistently across all threat models, regardless of the casing used in the source files.

author: nikolai3d
body:
This pull request introduces a complete, self-contained deployment workflow for deploying the app to a DigitalOcean Droplet (or any Ubuntu server) without relying on GitHub deploys. It adds all necessary scripts, configuration files, and documentation to build, package, transfer, and run the app on a remote server, including initial server setup, deployment automation, and reverse proxy configuration.

Deployment workflow and automation:

* Added `deploy.ps1`, a PowerShell script to build the app locally on Windows, bundle only the runtime files, upload them via SSH/SCP, and trigger a remote deployment script on the server. This script ensures only necessary files are transferred and automates the deployment process.
* Added `deploy_remote.sh`, a Bash script that runs on the server to extract the uploaded bundle, install production dependencies, and start or reload the app using PM2.

Server setup and configuration:

* Added `server-setup.sh`, a one-time Bash script to prepare a fresh Ubuntu server by creating a deploy user, hardening SSH, installing Node.js 20, PM2, Nginx, setting up a firewall, and configuring an Nginx reverse proxy for the app.
* Added `nginx.conf`, an example Nginx site configuration to reverse-proxy traffic to the Node.js app running on port 3000.

Documentation:

* Added a comprehensive `README.md` in the `deploy` folder, explaining prerequisites, setup steps, deployment commands, and optional HTTPS setup for a smooth deployment experience.

author: frikyfriky11
body:
This pull request introduces a comprehensive feature for importing bank statements and reconciling transactions within the application. It covers both backend processing and a user-friendly frontend interface.

**Key Features & Improvements:**

-   **Bank Statement Upload & Parsing:**
    -   Users can upload Excel files containing bank statements.
    -   A flexible backend parsing engine (using `IParser` and `IParsersFactory`) supports different bank statement formats (e.g., Sparkasse V1).
    -   Parsing results in the creation of `BankStatement` entities and associated `Transaction` records.
    -   Parsing warnings are now collected and displayed in a dedicated dialog for better user feedback.

-   **Transaction Reconciliation Workflow:**
    -   **Automated Status Assignment:** Imported transactions are automatically assigned a `PendingImportReview` status or flagged as `PotentialDuplicate` if a similar existing transaction is found.
    -   **Bank Statement Detail Page:** A new frontend page (`/bank-statements/:id`) allows users to review all transactions imported from a specific bank statement.
    -   **Unified "Complete" Action:** The `Transactions.Update` endpoint and the frontend's "Salva e Conferma" (now "Completa") button have been unified. This single action now handles saving data, confirming the transaction (changing its status to `Confirmed`), and clearing any duplicate flags, regardless of its initial pending or duplicate status.
    -   **Duplicate Resolution:** For `PotentialDuplicate` transactions, a dedicated inline `DuplicateResolver` component provides a side-by-side comparison with the existing transaction.
        -   Users can choose "È un duplicato (Elimina)" to permanently delete the newly imported duplicate transaction, simplifying the transaction list.
        -   Alternatively, they can choose "Completa" to proceed to the edit page and confirm the transaction as a new, valid entry.
    -   **"Undo" Import:** A new "Annulla Importazione" button on the Bank Statement Detail page allows users to delete an entire bank statement and all its associated transactions, providing a crucial undo mechanism.

-   **Technical Enhancements:**
    -   Improved data retrieval efficiency in backend handlers using projections (`.Select()`) instead of eager loading (`.Include()`).
    -   Introduced `CounterpartyIdentifier` for more robust automatic counterparty matching during import.
    -   Implemented pagination for the transaction list on the Bank Statement Detail page.
    -   Removed the `IgnoredImport` status and related logic, opting for direct deletion of unwanted duplicates to simplify application state and reduce maintenance overhead.
    -   Ensured consistent use of `useConfirm` for user confirmations.

This feature significantly streamlines the process of managing personal finances by automating transaction entry and providing clear tools for reconciliation.

body:
This PR implements a comprehensive Laravel blog application from scratch, transforming an empty repository into a fully-featured content management system. The application provides all the functionality specified in the requirements with a professional, responsive user interface.

## 🚀 What's New

### Complete Laravel Application Structure
- **Laravel 12.22.1** framework with full composer dependency management
- Proper MVC architecture following Laravel conventions
- Complete directory structure with all necessary configuration files
- Environment setup with `.env.example` template

### Database & Models
- **Posts table** with comprehensive schema including title, slug, content, excerpt, status, publication dates, and view counts
- **Post model** with automatic slug generation, scope methods, soft deletes, and intelligent excerpt creation
- **Database indexes** for optimal query performance
- **Sample data seeder** with 30+ realistic blog posts for immediate testing

### Full CRUD Implementation
- **PostController** with complete CRUD operations (Create, Read, Update, Delete)
- **Form validation** using dedicated Request classes with comprehensive rules
- **Route model binding** for clean URLs and automatic model resolution
- **Additional actions** like publish/unpublish, duplicate, and soft delete

### Professional User Interface
- **Responsive design** that works seamlessly on desktop, tablet, and mobile devices
- **Modern CSS** with custom styling, no external frameworks required
- **Intuitive navigation** with clear visual hierarchy and status indicators
- **Professional forms** with real-time validation feedback and user guidance

### Advanced Features
- **Full-text search** across post titles and content with highlighting
- **Advanced filtering** by status (draft/published), sorting options, and pagination controls
- **SEO optimization** with automatic meta tags, clean URLs, and proper heading structure
- **Post analytics** with view counting and reading time estimation
- **Related posts** suggestions for improved content discovery

## 🎯 Key Functionality Delivered

The application successfully addresses all requirements from the original issue:

### Core Blog Features
- Create new blog posts with rich content and metadata
- Edit existing posts with pre-populated forms and validation
- View individual posts with professional formatting and navigation
- Delete posts safely with soft delete functionality
- Manage post status (draft/published) with visual indicators

### Content Management
- Automatic slug generation from titles with uniqueness validation
- Intelligent excerpt creation from content when not provided
- Publication date scheduling for future releases
- Post duplication for creating similar content quickly
- View count tracking and reading time estimation

### Search & Navigation
- Powerful search functionality across all post content
- Filter posts by publication status and sort by various criteria
- Pagination with customizable results per page (10, 25, 50)
- Clear filter management with easy reset options
- Breadcrumb navigation and related post suggestions

### User Experience
- Mobile-first responsive design that adapts to all screen sizes
- Clean, modern interface with intuitive controls
- Real-time form validation with helpful error messages
- Success notifications and clear feedback for all actions
- Print-friendly post layouts for offline reading

## 🛠 Technical Implementation

### Security & Performance
- CSRF protection on all forms and state-changing operations
- Comprehensive input validation and sanitization
- XSS protection through proper output escaping
- Database query optimization with strategic indexing
- Efficient pagination to handle large post collections

### Code Quality
- PSR-12 coding standards compliance
- Laravel naming conventions throughout
- Comprehensive inline documentation
- Clean, maintainable code structure
- Proper error handling and edge case management

### Testing & Validation
- Updated existing tests to work with new routing structure
- Verified all CRUD operations work correctly
- Tested responsive design across multiple device sizes
- Validated search, filtering, and pagination functionality
- Confirmed SEO optimization and accessibility features

## 📱 Screenshots Included

The implementation includes visual verification of:
- Main blog index with search and filtering capabilities
- Professional post creation and editing forms
- Individual post views with all metadata and navigation
- Mobile-responsive design demonstrating cross-device compatibility

## 🎉 Ready for Production

This implementation provides a production-ready blog application with:
- Comprehensive documentation for setup and usage
- Sample data for immediate testing and demonstration
- Professional UI/UX suitable for public-facing websites
- Scalable architecture that can handle growth
- Modern web development best practices throughout

The application transforms the empty repository into a fully functional blog platform that exceeds the original requirements while maintaining clean, maintainable code and professional user experience.
